about: HITON-MB against Causal Explorer 1.5 on the paper's networks, sizes, and test; the release summary's HITON-MB entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 14 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch with hiton_mb and mmmb as merged, mmmb's default degrees_of_freedom='nonempty')
hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; the toolbox's fits and Andrey's ran in separate runs on shared nodes of the same CPU model, so the times are indicative
verdict_rule: per cell (network, rows; 20 datasets): per dataset, the mean over the targets both answered with a nonempty true set of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1) (an empty answer counts precision 1, distance 1) and of the set's F1; D = Andrey's minus Causal Explorer's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 was not rerun. A target where the toolbox stopped without an answer is left out of both sides
error_metric: set_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1); set_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of the set's F1. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members (the wrong answers of andrey.metrics.target_answer_scores), against the empty set's, the true set's size
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, every target of a dataset in one fit, no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit (3,600 s on Pigs), past which a fit is a timeout and never scored

claims.hiton_mb: Child, Insurance, Alarm, Hailfinder (every node a target) and Pigs (50 targets) at 200, 500, and 5,000 rows

seeds_note: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; a rerun holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39
cells_note: net:<network>:<rows>: forward samples of the bnlearn repository network, columns that hold one value left out of every fit, each answering the empty set at its target, every set scored against the whole network; gauss:<d>:<rows>[:<mean degree>]: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graph, standardized, mean degree 2 unless given (no reference: the toolbox reads categorical data only)
comparisons_note: judged: the method against the toolbox's at the method's claimed setting; the others are context, reported and never judged: hiton_mb and mmmb at the other's max_depth, iamb, inter_iamb, gs and pcmb at their defaults, and the other degrees-of-freedom rule
